methodology.remainingAssetsPoint: Exact arithmetic sum of the latest located figure for each of 41 active trusts: 13 from filed annual reports/quarterly filings (FY2025 annual reports or Q1 2026 quarterly) totaling $6,741,377,085, plus 28 from credible secondary compilations of trust annual reports (mostly FY2021-2022 as-of dates) totaling $10,004,759,262. This is a DOCUMENTED FLOOR, not a census: ~20 active trusts publish no retrievable figure and several secondary figures are dated 2021-2022, so the true current balance is higher.
methodology.remainingAssetsHigh: Upper bound consistent with: (a) ILR 'Dubious Distribution' (2018) ~$25B assets + ~$2B deferred obligations at YE2016, (b) >$1.5B of deferred obligations since funded (Honeywell $1.325B Jan 2023, RPM/Bondex, Western completed 2024), (c) net depletion of roughly $0.5B/yr since 2016, (d) PACER-only trusts carried at last-known values. Yields low-to-mid $20Bs; $22.5B is the midpoint estimate.

estimatedResidual.basis: No public inception-to-date payment figure exists for these trusts (DCPF-administered trusts report only to PACER). Allowance derived from: (1) system payout run-rate ~$1.5-2B/yr documented by Bates White/Mealey's ($14.0B paid 2006-2011) and RAND (~$3.3B in 2008) less the itemized components' share; (2) these trusts' combined documented balances (~$4B, corpus 1.1.2) vs combined initial funding, implying several billion paid to date; (3) corpus assessment that 2026 system-wide cumulative payments are 'plausibly $30B+'. Filed FY2024-FY2025 partial-year payments for Flintkote ($79,936,659) and B&W ($19,890,000) are conservatively treated inside this allowance and the B&W floor respectively.

bottomUpPayouts.methodology: Bottom-up sum replacing the round $24,000,000,000 point estimate. Tier 1: filed inception-to-date figures (14 trusts, as-of dates 2006-2026). Tier 2: secondary compilations citing filed annual reports (5 components), used only where no filed figure exists, each labeled. Tier 3: explicit allowance for ~25 trusts with no public cumulative figure, with stated range ($2.5-5B). The total is non-round because every component is a traceable number; it leans conservative because several Tier 1/2 as-of dates are stale (payments since those dates are only partly captured) and the B&W figure is a stated floor.
crossChecks: GAO-11-819 (2011): ~$17.5B paid on 3.3M claims, 1988-2010 — frozen 2011 baseline; consistent with this total after ~15 further years of payouts.
Bates White/Mealey's (via corpus dim12): $14.0B paid 2006-2011 alone.
Research corpus final report (dim12): 'cumulative payments by 2026 are plausibly $30B+'.
